gpu: lines 373-381 and 406-420, functions op_book and op_tools: build an NBT tree and malloc the rendered tag string inside the tick
lines 273, 311, 336, 351, 382, 423 and 461: list->r[list->n++] appends with no check against TRADES_MAX (32); add_with_check can overflow a list that grows past 32 recipes
line 432, function trades_add_default: a 32-recipe trade_list on the stack per call
lines 164-168: recipe stacks own heap tag strings (char* in a flat struct)
notes: The shuffle takes a separate Random (Collections.shuffle's shared static one), passed by the caller. Price tables and per-profession probabilities are hand-copied constants and are checked against the probe's manifest by test_trades.c per the header; not re-verified here. The price map lookup iterates a table in declared order, which does not matter since it is a keyed lookup. Java's price map field is named villagersSellingList (the header's comment says villagerStockList). trades_from_nbt: MerchantRecipeList(NBTTagCompound) for a villager's Offers and a snapshot's open trade window.
